target_customer: K-12 school districts and schools that pay for surveys and student support software
problem: Schools lacked good tools to gather and act on feedback from students, teachers and parents.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription sold to school districts
product_category: K-12 survey and student success analytics platform

founders.name: Aaron Feuer
founders.background_notes: As a high school senior in 2008 he was president of the California Association of Student Councils and helped draft California SB1422 (EdSurge, 2013-10).

founders.name: David Carel
founders.background_notes: Per the YC launch post, brought sports data tracking and analysis expertise.

founders.name: Xan Tanner
founders.background_notes: Named in the YC launch post.

competitors.name: SurveyMonkey
competitors.what: General survey tool; named in the YC launch post as the incumbent schools use

competitors.name: Harvard Graduate School of Education question bank
competitors.what: Free survey question bank for parent surveys

technical_complexity.rationale: Survey delivery plus analytics across thousands of schools; the harder parts were data integration and reporting.

defensibility.rationale: Longitudinal district survey data and district contracts create stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge; Panorama later bought smaller companies itself, such as Mesa Cloud in 2023 and Class Companion in 2025.

market_need_then: Founder experience with the California student survey law in 2008 and district demand; the YC launch post reports about 3,000 US schools using it.

rebrands.to: new tangram logo and deeper colors
rebrands.why: Visual refresh, name unchanged, per company blog.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known in K-12 edtech but not a consumer brand.

outcome_analysis: Panorama turned a founder's student government experience into a district sold survey platform. It raised a 2013 seed from Startup: Education, GV and others, then a $12M round in 2015, $16M in 2017 and a $60M Series C led by General Atlantic in 2021, and expanded through acquisitions of Mesa Cloud and Class Companion. Repeatable district sales and data stickiness explain the growth.
notes: The company's about page fetch was blocked by a rate limited safety check and was not retried. The $12M 2015 round label is not stated in the sources seen, so stage is other. The 2017 Series B label and amount come from EdWeek and aggregators; investors not found. Series C valuation not disclosed (an aggregator says $1.1B, unverified). Aggregate totals conflict ($76M to $92.7M). Founder prior employers not found.
